dish.title: Cider-Braised Pork Shoulder with Mustard Cabbage
dish.description: A long cider braise of pork shoulder, reduced to a spoon-coating sauce with apple, served with skillet mustard cabbage.

recipe_version.title: Cider-Braised Pork Shoulder with Mustard Cabbage
recipe_version.description: A long cider braise of pork shoulder, reduced to a spoon-coating sauce with apple, served with skillet mustard cabbage.

ingredients.name: boneless pork shoulder
ingredients.note: one piece, not pre-shredded and not sliced pork

ingredients.name: kosher salt
ingredients.note: divided: 2 tsp on the pork, 1/2 tsp on the cabbage

ingredients.name: olive oil
ingredients.note: divided: 1 tbsp to sear the pork, 1 tbsp for the cabbage

ingredients.name: apple
ingredients.preparation: cored and cut into 8 wedges each

ingredients.name: apple cider
ingredients.note: pasteurized apple cider, not apple cider vinegar and not hard cider

ingredients.name: water
ingredients.note: divided: 1/2 cup in the braise, 1/4 cup in the cabbage skillet

ingredients.name: dijon mustard
ingredients.note: store-bought; divided: 2 tbsp in the braise, 1 tbsp on the cabbage

ingredients.name: green cabbage
ingredients.note: 1 small head, cut into 8 wedges through the core so the wedges hold

steps.title: Heat the oven and season
steps.body: Heat the oven to 325 F. Pat the boneless pork shoulder dry. Season it on all sides with 2 tsp of the kosher salt and the black pepper. If the piece flaps into two thin tails, tie it with cotton kitchen twine. If it is already one compact piece, do not tie it. The twine is equipment, not an ingredient.

steps.title: Sear
steps.body: Set a Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Add 1 tbsp of the olive oil. Sear the boneless pork shoulder on all sides until deeply browned, about 8 minutes. Move the pork to a plate. Do not wipe out the fond.

steps.title: Build the braise
steps.body: Add the yellow onion, the apple wedges, the garlic, and the fresh thyme to the pot. Stir 4 minutes, until the onion softens. Add the apple cider, 1/2 cup of the water, and 2 tbsp of the dijon mustard. Return the pork. The liquid should come about halfway up the meat. If the pot is so wide that the liquid sits below one-third of the height, move to a smaller pot. Do not pour in a second carton of cider.

steps.title: Braise
steps.body: Cover and put the pot in the 325 F oven. Start checking at 2 hours 30 minutes. It is done at 2 hours 30 minutes to 2 hours 45 minutes, when the center is 195-203 F and a fork slides in with little resistance. The published cook time uses the long end, 2 hours 45 minutes. A shoulder that is tender at 2 hours 30 minutes finishes 15 minutes sooner. 145 F is not the target for this cut.

steps.title: Rest and reduce
steps.body: Move the boneless pork shoulder to a board and rest it 15 minutes. Discard the fresh thyme sprigs. While it rests, boil the pot liquid over medium-high until it coats a spoon, about 8 to 10 minutes. You want about 1 cup. Mash the soft apple into the sauce. Do not add flour. If a thick cap of fat is on the surface, skim it. This reduction shares the rest window with the cabbage and needs a second burner.

steps.title: Cook the cabbage
steps.body: During that same rest, heat a 12-inch skillet over medium. Add the remaining 1 tbsp olive oil. Lay in the 8 green cabbage wedges, cut side down, for 3 minutes, until the cut face browns. Turn them. Add the remaining 1/4 cup water, the apple cider vinegar, the remaining 1 tbsp dijon mustard, and the remaining 1/2 tsp kosher salt. Cover 4 minutes, until the core is tender to a knife. Uncover if the skillet is watery. One burner instead of two adds about 10 minutes after the sauce; the published total is the two-burner clock.

steps.title: Slice and serve
steps.body: Remove any twine. If the boneless pork shoulder holds, cut 1/2-inch slices against the grain. If it collapses, pull large chunks. Do not puree it and do not shred it into a fine pile. Spoon the cider sauce and the soft apple over the pork. Sprinkle the fresh parsley. Serve the green cabbage wedges beside the meat. No bread and no potatoes.

recipe_version.heat: Sear on the stove over medium-high, then a covered oven braise at 325 F. Sauce reduces at a boil. Cabbage skillet is medium.
recipe_version.doneness: Pork shoulder at 195-203 F in the center and fork-tender. 145 F is not done for this cut. Rest 15 minutes. Slice 1/2 inch against the grain if it holds; pull large chunks if it collapses. Do not puree it.

curator_preflight.detail: Every listed ingredient name is used. Water is split 1/2 cup braise and 1/4 cup cabbage. Dijon is split 2 tbsp and 1 tbsp. Apple stays in the sauce. Thyme is discarded after the braise.
Olive oil is 2 tbsp, 1 tbsp for the sear and 1 tbsp for the cabbage. The sauce is not finished with butter.

Cider-mustard sauce is built and reduced from cider, water, store-bought dijon mustard, onion, apple, garlic, and thyme. No flour thickener and no unnamed spice blend. Mustard cabbage is the second component.

Prep 20 + cook 192 = 212. Cook is 8 sear + 4 aromatics + 165 oven (the long end) + 15 rest. Reduction and cabbage run inside that rest on two burners. One burner adds about 10 minutes and is not the published total.
Liquid, apple, thyme, and cabbage wedges do not quarter cleanly. Doneness and oven temperature do not scale.
contains_meat true. contains_poultry false (no chicken stock). contains_dairy false. allergens is empty. dairy_free is unconditional. HH001 is false because of pork.

scaling_notes.1: Buy about 1 lb boneless pork shoulder in one chunk, not thin cutlets. Braising liquid has a floor: 1 cup apple cider and 1/4 cup water in the pot, even though a strict quarter of the written liquid is less. Below that the pot scorches. Cabbage water: 1 tbsp. Use 1 small apple, not a quarter of an apple. Two thyme sprigs, not a fraction of a sprig. Two cabbage wedges from a small head; the rest of the head is not part of this scaled recipe. Dijon: 2 tsp in the pot and 1 tsp on the cabbage. Oven stays 325 F. Target stays 195-203 F. Time does not quarter: plan about 1 hour 45 minutes to 2 hours in the oven for a 1 lb piece of similar thickness.
scaling_notes.2: 1.5 lb in one piece. Liquid floor: 1 1/4 cups apple cider and 1/3 cup water in the pot, not a strict half, if the Dutch oven is wide. Cabbage water: 2 tbsp. One apple. Two thyme sprigs. Four cabbage wedges. Halve the salt, pepper, oil, and dijon (1 tbsp in the pot, 1 1/2 tsp on the cabbage). Oven 325 F and 195-203 F do not change. Oven time is about 2 hours 15 minutes, not half of 2 hours 45 minutes.
scaling_notes.4: As written. 3 lb is about 12 oz raw per person before the braise shrinks it. Liquid is 2 cups cider plus 1/2 cup water in the pot and 1/4 cup water in the skillet.
do_not_scale: the rule that the liquid must reach about halfway up the meat

coverage_contribution: First real braise. Pork is absent from the live 24 and from the three DR1 drafts (beef, chicken, mussels). The reduced cider-mustard sauce and the mustard cabbage are compounds. The liquid floor, the one-piece shoulder, counted wedges and apples, and divided mustard, oil, salt, and water are the scaling stress. Not HH001.
